exercises.question: A and B are partners. A's capital is ₹40,000 and B's capital is ₹20,000. Profit for the year is ₹30,000. Partnership deed is silent on interest on capital and profit-sharing. Show how profit will be distributed.
exercises.solution:
Since the partnership deed is silent:
1. Interest on capital is not allowed.
2. Profits are shared equally.

Distribution:
• A's share = ₹30,000 / 2 = ₹15,000
• B's share = ₹30,000 / 2 = ₹15,000

exercises.question: Calculate interest on drawings of Partner Ashok @ 10% p.a. if he withdrew ₹2,000 per month in the beginning of each month for the year.
exercises.solution:
Total annual drawings = ₹2,000 × 12 = ₹24,000.
Average period for beginning of every month = 78/12 months (6.5 months).
Interest = ₹24,000 × (10 / 100) × (78 / 12) = ₹1,560.

exercises.question: Net profit of a firm is ₹75,000. Manager is entitled to a commission of 10% *after* charging such commission. Calculate manager's commission.
Distinguish between Fixed Capital Method and Fluctuating Capital Method (Any 2 points).
exercises.solution:
1. Number of Accounts: Under Fixed method, two accounts (Capital and Current) are maintained. Under Fluctuating method, only one account (Capital Account) is maintained.
2. Balance fluctuation: Capital balance remains unchanged year after year in Fixed method, whereas it fluctuates every year in the Fluctuating method.

exercises.question: State any two essential elements of a partnership firm.
exercises.solution:
1. Agreement: There must be an agreement (written or oral) between all partners.
2. Business and Profit Sharing: The agreement must be to carry on a lawful business with the objective of earning and sharing profits.
